topics:
  - id: pet
    color: "#FFAABB"
    name: PET
    icon: images/icons/pet.svg
    subtitle: tau subtypes & spread
    text:
      - "Alzheimer's disease does not unfold the same way in everyone. Using tau-PET imaging and
        disease progression modelling, we discovered that tau spreads through the brain along four
        distinct trajectories: limbic, MTL-sparing, posterior and lateral temporal."
      - "Tau does not appear everywhere at once: it travels along the brain's connections. By
        modelling this spread on brain networks we can explain where tau appears, and we now build
        personalised models that forecast how each person's disease may evolve."
    papers:
      - lead: Jacob Vogel
        photo: members/images/round/jake.jpg
        journal: Nature Medicine
        date: "Apr 29, 2021"
        title: "Four distinct trajectories of tau deposition identified in Alzheimer's disease"
        url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01309-6
        summary: "Using tau-PET scans from 1,612 individuals, we identified four distinct trajectories of tau
          pathology: limbic, MTL-sparing, posterior and lateral temporal. These subtypes were stable over
          follow-up, replicated in a separate sample with a different radiotracer, and showed distinct
          demographic and cognitive profiles and outcomes, suggesting a re-examination of the idea of
          'typical' Alzheimer's disease."
        credit: "Figures adapted from this paper."
        figures:
          - {src: images/news/vogel2021_subtypes.jpg, label: "Four tau subtypes", alt: "Brain maps of tau in the limbic, MTL-sparing, posterior and lateral temporal subtypes, with a plot of how individuals fall across the four subtypes"}
          - {src: images/news/vogel2021_stages.jpg, label: "Subtypes across disease stages", alt: "Brain maps showing how tau builds up in each of the four subtypes across model stages"}
          - {src: images/news/vogel2021_epicenters.jpg, label: "Modelling spread from epicenters", alt: "Plots and brain maps comparing observed and predicted tau from epicenter regions in each subtype"}
  - id: fmri
    color: "#77AADD"
    name: fMRI
    icon: images/icons/fmri.svg
    subtitle: brain networks
    text:
      - "Brain communication is organised along several axes that shape how resources are
        distributed from moment to moment, and may underlie key cognitive processes. Using a
        whole-brain framework, we found that ageing reshapes communication along one of these axes,
        while Alzheimer's disease affects an entirely different one."
    papers:
      - lead: Jonathan Rittmo
        photo: members/images/round/jon.jpg
        journal: Nature Neuroscience
        date: "Oct 1, 2026"
        title: "Different functional connectivity gradients reflect aging and Alzheimer's disease"
        url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41593-026-02402-0
        summary: "In two independent cohorts (BioFINDER-2, N = 973; ADNI, N = 129), functional connectivity
          changes linked to aging and to Alzheimer's disease aligned with separate axes of brain
          communication. Early AD pathology and later cognitive decline followed the sensory-association
          axis, while age-related change followed the representation-executive axis across the adult
          lifespan."
        credit: "Figures from this paper."
        figures:
          - {src: images/news/rittmo2026_axes.jpg, label: "Age and AD along separate axes", alt: "Brain maps and scatter plots relating age and AD pathology to the sensory-association and representation-executive axes"}
          - {src: images/news/rittmo2026_pathology.jpg, label: "Across the pathology score", alt: "Plots of the correlation with the sensory-association axis and of pathology measures across the pathology score"}

  - id: omics
    color: "#44BB99"
    name: Omics
    icon: images/icons/omics.svg
    subtitle: proteomics & single-cell
    text:
      - "Every cell type in the brain responds to Alzheimer's disease in its own way. Using
        single-nucleus RNA sequencing, we found a coordinated, multi-cellular response to AD pathology
        in one dataset and replicated it cleanly in a completely independent one: a reference point for
        future perturbation and drug-development studies."
      - "We bring the same care for robustness to proteins: spinal-fluid reference proteins make
        biomarkers more accurate and easier to interpret."
    papers:
      - lead: Gabriele Vilkaite
        photo: members/images/round/gabi.jpg
        journal: bioRxiv
        date: "Oct 23, 2026"
        title: "A coordinated and reproducible multicellular response to AD pathology"
        url: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.19.759610
        summary: "Single-cell studies of the Alzheimer's brain often report differing results and rarely
          consider how cell types respond together. Across 2.3 million nuclei from 427 ROSMAP donors, we
          identified multicellular signatures of AD pathology and of sex, including profound changes in
          RORB-GABRG excitatory neurons and disrupted oligodendrocyte precursor signalling. These
          signatures predicted neuropathology and sex in a fully independent dataset (SEA-AD), giving a
          baseline against which perturbation and treatment experiments can be compared."
        credit: "Figures from this paper (CC BY-NC 4.0)."
        figures:
          - {src: images/news/vilkaite2026_workflow.jpg, label: "Analysis workflow", alt: "Overview of the analysis workflow, from single-cell data to robust gene clusters"}
          - {src: images/news/vilkaite2026_cohorts.jpg, label: "Discovery and validation", alt: "Results in the ROSMAP discovery cohort and the SEA-AD validation cohort"}
          - {src: images/news/vilkaite2026_network.jpg, label: "Cell-to-cell communication", alt: "Communication networks between brain cell types"}

  - id: ai
    color: "#EEDD88"
    name: AI
    icon: images/icons/ai.svg
    subtitle: machine learning
    text:
      - "We use machine learning and deep learning to diagnose dementias from proteins, and to
        predict or even generate tau-PET scans from cheaper, more widely available data such as MRI
        and blood tests."
      - "We also hold these models to a high standard: we have shown how data leakage makes
        models <em>look</em> better while they actually generalise worse, and built tools to prevent
        it."
    papers:
      - lead: Lijun An
        photo: members/images/round/lijun.jpg
        journal: Nature Medicine
        date: "Mar 31, 2026"
        title: "A deep joint-learning proteomics model for diagnosis of six conditions associated with dementia"
        url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-026-04303-y
        summary: "Mixed pathologies make dementia hard to diagnose, and scalable biomarkers are missing for most of
          them. We present ProtAIDe-Dx, a deep joint-learning model trained on 17,187 patients and controls that
          uses plasma proteomics to diagnose six conditions at once, with a balanced accuracy of 70-95%. It
          improved differential diagnosis in a memory clinic sample and shows which proteins drive each
          person's result, all from a single blood draw."
        credit: "Figures adapted from this paper (CC BY 4.0)."
        figures:
          - {src: images/news/an2026_workflow.jpg, label: "Model workflow", alt: "Workflow of the ProtAIDe-Dx model, from plasma proteins through a neural network to disease probabilities and an individual risk report"}
          - {src: images/news/an2026_performance.jpg, label: "Performance and validation", alt: "Plots of diagnostic performance across conditions, with APOE, cognition and cognitive decline validation"}
          - {src: images/news/an2026_subgroups.jpg, label: "Probability map and subgroups", alt: "Maps of individuals by diagnostic probability, with clusters and subgroup characteristics"}

      permutation to test whether a pipeline performs above chance when no true signal is present."
    links:
      - {label: "Get the package", url: "https://pypi.org/project/Leakly/"}
      - {label: "Source code", url: "https://github.com/DeMONLab-BioFINDER/Leakly"}
  - name: Plumber
    text: "A web tool for checking data leakage using large language models. Paste a method section,
      select the leakage checks, and it builds a structured review prompt to copy into an LLM."
    links:

```{r chapters, echo=FALSE}
# Builds the theme tiles and one chapter per theme from the `topics` list above.
# Chapters are <article> elements, not <section>: see the note on the theme's
# section:target rule in README.md ("Research page").
library(htmltools)

topics <- rmarkdown::metadata$topics

tile <- function(t) {
  a(class = "research-tile", href = paste0("#", t$id), style = paste0("--topic:", t$color),
    span(class = "theme-icon", img(src = t$icon, alt = "")),
    span(class = "tile-name", span(class = "tile-key", t$name), br(), t$subtitle))
}

# one paper's figures, shown one at a time, with buttons if there are several
stage <- function(p, stage_id, active) {
  many <- length(p$figures) > 1
  div(class = "spot-stage", id = stage_id, hidden = if (!active) NA,
      `aria-roledescription` = if (many) "carousel", `aria-label` = paste("Figures:", p$title),
      div(class = "spot-frames",
          Map(function(f, i) {
            a(class = paste("spot-frame", if (i == 1) "active"), href = f$src, target = "_blank",
              `data-label` = f$label,
              img(src = f$src, alt = f$alt, loading = "lazy"))
          }, p$figures, seq_along(p$figures))),
      div(class = "spot-bar",
          span(class = "spot-label", `aria-live` = "polite", p$figures[[1]]$label),
          if (many)
            div(class = "spot-controls",
                tags$button(type = "button", class = "spot-pause", `aria-label` = "Pause figures",
                            tags$i(class = "bi bi-pause-fill", `aria-hidden` = "true")),
                tags$button(type = "button", class = "spot-prev", `aria-label` = "Previous figure",
                            tags$i(class = "bi bi-chevron-left", `aria-hidden` = "true")),
                lapply(seq_along(p$figures), function(i) {
                  tags$button(type = "button", class = paste("spot-dot", if (i == 1) "active"),
                              `aria-label` = paste("Show figure", i))
                }),
                tags$button(type = "button", class = "spot-next", `aria-label` = "Next figure",
                            tags$i(class = "bi bi-chevron-right", `aria-hidden` = "true")))),
      div(class = "spot-credit", p$credit))
}

# one paper in the list; with several papers, opening one shows its figures
paper <- function(p, stage_id, active, several) {
  body_id <- paste0(stage_id, "-text")
  head <- tagList(img(class = "spot-photo", src = p$photo, alt = ""),
                  span(class = "spot-head-text",
                       span(class = "spot-title", p$title),
                       span(class = "spot-meta", paste0(p$lead, " et al. "), HTML("&middot; "),
                            em(p$journal), HTML(" &middot; "), p$date)))
  div(class = paste("spot-paper", if (active) "open"),
      tags$h3(class = "spot-heading",
              if (several)
                tags$button(type = "button", class = "spot-head", `data-stage` = stage_id,
                            `aria-expanded` = if (active) "true" else "false",
                            `aria-controls` = body_id, head)
              else
                div(class = "spot-head", head)),
      div(class = "spot-body", id = body_id, hidden = if (!active) NA,
          tags$p(p$summary),
          a(class = "spot-link", href = p$url, target = "_blank", "Read the paper",
            tags$i(class = "bi bi-arrow-up-right", `aria-hidden` = "true"))))
}

chapter <- function(t, i) {
  ids <- paste0(t$id, "-", seq_along(t$papers))
  several <- length(t$papers) > 1
  tags$article(
    id = t$id, style = paste0("--topic:", t$color),
    class = paste("spot-chapter reveal", if (i %% 2 == 0) "flip"),
    div(class = "spot-top",
        span(class = "theme-icon", img(src = t$icon, alt = "")),
        div(tags$h2(class = "spot-name", t$name), div(class = "spot-subtitle", t$subtitle))),
    div(class = "spot-intro", lapply(t$text, function(x) tags$p(HTML(x)))),
    div(class = "spot-grid",
        div(class = "spot-stages",
            Map(function(p, id, k) stage(p, id, k == 1), t$papers, ids, seq_along(ids))),
        div(class = "spot-papers",
            Map(function(p, id, k) paper(p, id, k == 1, several), t$papers, ids, seq_along(ids)))))
}

tool <- function(s) {
  div(class = "software-card",
      tags$h3(class = "software-name", s$name),
      tags$p(s$text),
      div(class = "software-links",
          lapply(s$links, function(l) a(href = l$url, target = "_blank", l$label))))
}

tagList(
  tags$nav(class = "research-tiles", `aria-label` = "Research themes",
           lapply(topics, tile),
           a(class = "research-tile software-tile", href = "#software",
             span(class = "theme-icon", img(src = "images/icons/software.svg", alt = "")),
             span(class = "tile-name", span(class = "tile-key", "Software"), br(), "open tools"))),
  Map(chapter, topics, seq_along(topics)),
  tags$article(id = "software", class = "software reveal",
               div(class = "spot-top",
                   span(class = "theme-icon", img(src = "images/icons/software.svg", alt = "")),
                   div(tags$h2(class = "spot-name", "Software"),
                       div(class = "spot-subtitle", "open tools from the lab"))),
               div(class = "software-grid", lapply(rmarkdown::metadata$software, tool))),
  div(class = "icon-credit", HTML(rmarkdown::metadata$icon_credit))
)
```

```{=html}
<script>
// Figure displays: each one moves through its paper's figures while it is on
// screen. Hovering or focusing it holds the current figure, and the pause button
// stops it. People who prefer reduced motion get no automatic changes.
// Chapters fade in as they scroll into view.
(function () {
  var still = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  var seconds = 5;

  document.querySelectorAll(".spot-stage").forEach(function (box) {
    var frames = box.querySelectorAll(".spot-frame");
    var label = box.querySelector(".spot-label");
    var dots = box.querySelectorAll(".spot-dot");
    var pause = box.querySelector(".spot-pause");
    var current = 0, held = false, onScreen = false, paused = still;
    if (frames.length < 2) return;

    function show(n) {
      current = (n + frames.length) % frames.length;
      frames.forEach(function (f, k) { f.classList.toggle("active", k === current); });
      dots.forEach(function (d, k) { d.classList.toggle("active", k === current); });
      label.textContent = frames[current].dataset.label;
    }
    function setPaused(value) {
      paused = value;
      pause.setAttribute("aria-label", paused ? "Play figures" : "Pause figures");
      pause.querySelector("i").className = "bi " + (paused ? "bi-play-fill" : "bi-pause-fill");
    }

    setPaused(still);
    box.querySelector(".spot-prev").addEventListener("click", function () { show(current - 1); });
    box.querySelector(".spot-next").addEventListener("click", function () { show(current + 1); });
    dots.forEach(function (d, k) { d.addEventListener("click", function () { show(k); }); });
    pause.addEventListener("click", function () { setPaused(!paused); });
    ["mouseenter", "focusin"].forEach(function (e) { box.addEventListener(e, function () { held = true; }); });
    ["mouseleave", "focusout"].forEach(function (e) { box.addEventListener(e, function () { held = false; }); });

    if ("IntersectionObserver" in window) {
      new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
        onScreen = entries[0].isIntersecting;
      }, { threshold: 0.4 }).observe(box);
    } else {
      onScreen = true;
    }
    setInterval(function () {
      if (!paused && !held && onScreen && !box.hidden && !document.hidden) show(current + 1);
    }, seconds * 1000);
  });

  // Papers in a chapter: opening one shows its text and its figures.
  document.querySelectorAll(".spot-chapter").forEach(function (chapter) {
    var heads = chapter.querySelectorAll("button.spot-head");
    heads.forEach(function (head) {
      head.addEventListener("click", function () {
        heads.forEach(function (h) {
          var open = h === head;
          h.setAttribute("aria-expanded", open);
          h.closest(".spot-paper").classList.toggle("open", open);
          document.getElementById(h.getAttribute("aria-controls")).hidden = !open;
          document.getElementById(h.dataset.stage).hidden = !open;
        });
      });
    });
  });

  var chapters = document.querySelectorAll(".research-page .reveal");
  if (still || !("IntersectionObserver" in window)) {
    chapters.forEach(function (c) { c.classList.add("visible"); });
    return;
  }
  var seen = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
    entries.forEach(function (e) {
      if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.classList.add("visible"); seen.unobserve(e.target); }
    });
  }, { threshold: 0.1 });
  chapters.forEach(function (c) { seen.observe(c); });
})();
</script>
```
